guardrail: Research is hypothesis generation only. No item in this file is allowed to change live predictions until separately validated.
research_summary: Evidence supports testing continuation versus reversal as a state-dependent process: information, volume, liquidity, VWAP distance, time of day, and prior intraday structure jointly matter. Small-cap and low-priced stocks require explicit spread, depth, turnover, and execution-cost controls. Motif discovery should use chronological discovery, frozen definitions, and later out-of-sample validation.

hypotheses.title: Volume-climax pullback predicts bounce decay
hypotheses.claim: After an impulse with extreme relative volume, each subsequent reclaim attempt has smaller median upside and higher failure probability when pullback volume contracts but spread and volatility remain elevated.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Separates genuine absorption and continuation from exhaustion-driven rebounds.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 5-minute and 30-minute return, maximum favorable excursion, maximum adverse excursion, and time to failure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Larger climax volume and later bounce number should predict lower bounce size and greater downside failure risk, especially with wide spreads.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Chronological event study with clustered standard errors; compare first, second, and third bounces using matched impulse magnitude and liquidity buckets.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Stable monotonic decay across at least three non-overlapping time periods and economically meaningful improvement after estimated spread and slippage costs.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No monotonic bounce decay, instability across regimes, or disappearance after controlling for impulse size and liquidity.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Failed reclaim and lower-high structure forecast downside acceleration
hypotheses.claim: A bounce that fails below the impulse high and forms a lower high has higher probability of a rapid 5% or 10% falloff when price also loses VWAP or the pullback low.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Provides a measurable distinction between a quick technical bounce and renewed directional weakness.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of 5% and 10% decline, time-to-threshold, and maximum drawdown over 15, 30, and 60 minutes.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Lower highs combined with failed VWAP reclaims should increase downside probability and shorten time-to-failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Event-time survival analysis with competing upside-threshold outcomes and ticker/date clustered bootstrap confidence intervals.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive hazard-ratio separation with calibrated probabilities and confidence intervals excluding no effect in at least two unseen periods.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Effect vanishes after volatility normalization, is driven by a few tickers, or cannot predict beyond a simple return-minus-VWAP baseline.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Liquidity-adjusted VWAP behavior distinguishes continuation from exhaustion
hypotheses.claim: A move far above VWAP is more likely to continue when traded value and depth expand with the move, but more likely to mean-revert when price extension coincides with declining depth, wider spreads, and negative order-flow confirmation.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: VWAP distance alone is ambiguous; liquidity participation may identify whether price discovery or temporary imbalance dominates.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of making a new intraday high within 10 minutes versus reverting to VWAP or the prior consolidation midpoint.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Expansion in turnover and depth should favor continuation; spread widening and depth deterioration should favor exhaustion.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Two-way classification event study with purged walk-forward logistic or gradient-boosted models and transaction-cost-adjusted evaluation.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Out-of-sample rank-ordering improvement over VWAP distance alone, with stable calibration and positive net information coefficient after costs.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No incremental value from depth/spread variables, poor calibration, or results dependent on quote artifacts or locked/crossed markets.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Catalyst, float, and turnover jointly shape impulse persistence
hypotheses.claim: Catalyst-driven stocks with low float and unusually high turnover exhibit stronger initial continuation but also higher exhaustion and reversal risk when turnover peaks early and fails to reaccelerate.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Small-cap momentum is likely heterogeneous rather than universally persistent.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 30-minute return, probability of new high, and probability of 5% adverse move after the first pullback.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Low-float/high-turnover catalysts should produce larger early moves; early turnover climax without later expansion should predict sharper failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Stratified event study by catalyst and float quintile, followed by out-of-sample interaction-model validation.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Consistent interaction effects across catalyst categories and years, with net outcomes surviving realistic spread and latency assumptions.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Effects disappear after controlling for gap, volatility, or market-wide small-cap momentum; catalyst labels show material timestamp leakage.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Step-plateau-reacceleration is a distinct multi-session state
hypotheses.claim: After a catalyst-driven step-up, multi-session consolidation above the prior level followed by expanding turnover and a close near the session high predicts greater next-session continuation than a single-session breakout of similar size.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Tests whether price acceptance and delayed participation create a repeatable continuation regime.
features_to_test: number of closes above prior resistance
hypotheses.target_outcome: Next-session high extension, close-to-close return, and probability of breaking the plateau high within the first hour.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Stable higher-level acceptance plus renewed turnover should predict continuation; declining closes and turnover should predict failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Session-level event study with overlapping-event controls, purged walk-forward validation, and separate discovery and confirmation samples.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive forward-return spread in multiple later calendar blocks with confidence intervals surviving gap, volatility, and liquidity controls.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No incremental effect over prior-session return and volume, or performance is concentrated in one historic catalyst episode.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Leakage-safe unnamed motif discovery
hypotheses.claim: Unsupervised discovery of normalized price-volume motifs or change-point states can identify recurring intraday structures with stable forward outcomes without relying on predefined setups.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: May uncover useful sequences that named pattern rules miss, while testing whether the structure generalizes rather than fitting folklore.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Cluster-conditional forward return, new-high probability, 5% downside probability, and time-to-failure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Some motifs should show asymmetric continuation or failure outcomes, but direction must be determined only after discovery.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Use an early chronological discovery window for matrix-profile, shapelet, clustering, or hidden-state discovery; freeze motifs and labels; validate only on later unseen dates with purged gaps and multiple-testing correction.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Motif outcome remains significant in at least two later chronological blocks, survives nearest-neighbor and simple-feature benchmarks, and retains economic value after costs.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Motifs drift materially, require future normalization, fail on later dates, or lose significance after correcting for the number of discovered patterns.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

important_caveats: Intraday data require strict timestamp alignment, realistic quote/trade sequencing, and exclusion of halted, locked, crossed, and clearly stale observations.
Use point-in-time float, shares outstanding, corporate-action adjustments, and catalyst timestamps; avoid survivorship and delisting bias.
Normalize volume, volatility, VWAP distance, and spreads by ticker and time of day before pooling securities.
Report conditional distributions, not only mean returns; include 5% and 10% adverse excursions, time-to-failure, hit rates, and calibration.
Validation must be chronological, preferably with purging and embargoes for overlapping horizons; model selection and threshold selection belong inside training windows.
Small-cap results can be dominated by execution costs, price-limit behavior, halts, borrow constraints, and a small number of extreme observations.
research_gaps: How do halt reopenings alter second- and third-bounce failure severity?
Which news-taxonomy features best distinguish durable information from promotional or low-quality catalysts?
Do order-book imbalance and queue depletion improve prediction beyond trades, spreads, and depth summaries?

Can hierarchical or transfer-learning models share information across sparse low-float names without creating cross-ticker leakage?
